name: make_claims
command:
import os,resource; os.sched_setaffinity(0,sorted(os.sched_getaffinity(0))[:2]); resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_CPU,(115,115)); resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_AS,(6*1024**3,6*1024**3));
import json
claims=[
("C01","The target is MathDB 382297, the bunkbed conjecture BBC(E7,T_n) for the transitive tournament.","inputs/literal382297.json","statement field","The statement field begins 'Let T_n be the transitive tournament on n vertices' and states 'BBC(E7,T_n) holds for T_n'."),
("C02","MathDB records the target as open.","inputs/literal382297.json","status field","\"status\": \"open\"; \"solutions\": []."),
("C03","Kasteleyn introduced the bunkbed conjecture in 1985.","inputs/sources/bunkbed-acyclic.txt","Section 1, Introduction","'The Bunkbed Conjecture, introduced by Kasteleyn in 1985 [9, Remark 5]'."),
("C04","The undirected bunkbed conjecture is false in general.","inputs/sources/bunkbed-acyclic.txt","Section 1, Introduction","'This conjecture was disproved by Gladkov, Pak and Zimin [2]'."),
("C05","E7 in arXiv:2406.01790v1 is renamed D7 in the published journal version at the same numbered locations.","inputs/author-CANDIDATE.md","Exact semantic endpoint and sources","'This is E7 in arXiv:2406.01790v1, Definition 1.4, Model 4.5, Conjecture 6.4, and D7 in the published European Journal of Combinatorics 128 (2025), 104188, same numbered locations.'"),
("C06","D7 is the unconditioned directed model: a uniform subset of the doubled digraph's edges is retained.","inputs/sources/bunkbed-journal.txt","Model 4.5 (D7(D); Unconditioned Digraphs)","'For a directed multigraph D, let F subset E(D-tilde) be chosen uniformly at random amongst all such subsets. Keep precisely these edges, and discard the others.'"),
("C07","Hollom's Theorem 1.6 says BBC(D7(D)) is false for suitable directed multigraphs.","inputs/sources/bunkbed-journal.txt","Theorem 1.6 and Section 5.2","'there are counterexamples to the statement BBC(E(Q)) for each of the models ... D7(D)'; Section 5.2 constructs the directed multigraph."),
("C08","Hollom's Question 6.3 asks whether BBC(D7(D)) holds for all acyclic digraphs.","inputs/sources/bunkbed-journal.txt","Section 6","'Question 6.3. Do BBC(D6(D,T,F)) and BBC(D7(D)) hold for all acyclic digraphs D?'"),
("C09","Hollom writes that the acyclic question seems unclear and that the induction is far from trivial.","inputs/sources/bunkbed-journal.txt","Section 6","'It seems unclear to the author whether the answer to Question 6.3 should be positive or negative. Indeed, this problem is far more amenable to inductive techniques than the case of graphs with cycles, but actually performing this induction seems far from trivial.'"),
("C10","Conjecture 6.4 asserts BBC(D7(T_n)) for the transitive tournament.","inputs/sources/bunkbed-journal.txt","Section 6, Conjecture 6.4","'Conjecture 6.4. BBC(D7(Tn)) holds for Tn, the transitive tournament on n vertices.'"),
("C11","Hollom calls the tournament case approachable but more difficult than expected.","inputs/sources/bunkbed-journal.txt","Section 6","'one case that does seem approachable, though was found by the author to be more difficult than expected'."),
("C12","Hollom says the complete-graph techniques do not directly apply because T_n lacks K_n's symmetries.","inputs/sources/bunkbed-journal.txt","Section 6","'these do not directly apply, in short because Tn does not have the same symmetries as Kn'."),
("C13","van Hintum and Lammers proved the undirected complete graph case.","inputs/sources/bunkbed-complete-correct.txt","Title and abstract","'The bunkbed conjecture on the complete graph'; abstract: 'This paper settles the conjecture in the case of a constant percolation parameter and G the complete graph.'"),
("C14","Przybylowski's Theorem 1.2 gives a simple acyclic digraph with P(u- -> v-) < P(u- -> v+).","inputs/sources/bunkbed-acyclic.txt","Theorem 1.2","'There is a simple acyclic directed graph with distinguished vertices u, v such that P_{1/2}(u- -> v-) < P_{1/2}(u- -> v+).'"),
("C15","Przybylowski's result resolves the conjectures of Leander and Hollom.","inputs/sources/bunkbed-acyclic.txt","Abstract and Section 1","Abstract: 'thereby resolving conjectures posed by Leander and by Hollom.'"),
("C16","Przybylowski's graph has missing adjacencies and is not a tournament.","inputs/second-review-REVIEW.md","Section 2","'Its sparse G1 and its post-forcing gadgets have missing adjacencies and multiple entrances.' The acyclic source calls it a 'simple acyclic directed graph' (Theorem 1.2), not a tournament."),
("C17","T_n has vertex set {0,...,n-1} and arcs i->j exactly for i<j.","inputs/author-CANDIDATE.md","Exact semantic endpoint and sources","'the transitive tournament T_n, whose arcs are i->j for i<j'."),
("C18","There are n(n-1) horizontal tokens plus n vertical tokens, n^2 in total.","inputs/lean/BunFinalModel.lean","theorem card_htoken and theorem card_token","card_htoken: Fintype.card (HToken n) = n * (n - 1); card_token: Fintype.card (Token n) = n * n. Second review: 'n(n-1) horizontal tokens plus n vertical tokens, n^2 in total.'"),
("C19","The outcome space has 2^(n*n) elements.","inputs/lean/BunFinalModel.lean","theorem card_out","theorem card_out (n : Nat) : Fintype.card (Out n) = 2 ^ (n * n)."),
("C20","Reach is the reflexive-transitive closure of the enabled-arc relation, so the zero-length path counts.","inputs/lean/BunkbedBase.lean","def Reach","def Reach (n : Nat) (ω : Out n) (x y : Vert n) : Prop := Relation.ReflTransGen (Arc n ω) x y. Author proposal: 'Reach includes a length-zero path.'"),
("C21","The proof reveals prefixes P(u), P(u+1), ... and tracks R0(k), R1(k) with counts A(k), B(k).","inputs/author-CANDIDATE.md","Full ordinary proof","'For a prefix ending at k>=u, let R_k^0,R_k^1 be the sets of indices in [u,k] whose copies are reachable ... and put A_k=|R_k^0|, B_k=|R_k^1|.'"),
("C22","Reachability of a vertex of index at most k is final for the prefix P(k).","inputs/author-CANDIDATE.md","Full ordinary proof","'The prefix restriction does not change reachability of any vertex in it, since a directed path cannot return from a larger index.'"),
("C23","The initial law at k=u is (1,0) with probability 1/2 and (1,1) with probability 1/2.","inputs/author-CANDIDATE.md","Full ordinary proof","'At k=u, the distribution of (A_k,B_k) is (1,0) with probability 1/2 and (1,1) with probability 1/2.'"),
("C24","The increment uses independent X,Y,Z with U = X or (Z and Y), V = Y or (Z and X).","inputs/author-CANDIDATE.md","Full ordinary proof","'Let Z be the new vertical-edge bit, independent and fair. Exactly the new reachable indicators are U = X or (Z and Y), V = Y or (Z and X).'"),
("C25","The four increment probabilities are qr, (1-q)r/2, q(1-r)/2 and 1-(q+r)/2.","inputs/shortest-proof-PROOF.md","Detailed independent checks","'For increments (0,0),(1,0),(0,1),(1,1), the four probabilities are qr, (1-q)r/2, q(1-r)/2, 1-(q+r)/2.'"),
("C26","Count sufficiency uses completeness in the order: every earlier vertex is a predecessor of the new vertex.","inputs/shortest-proof-PROOF.md","Shortest proof","'This law depends only on counts: every earlier vertex is a predecessor of the new vertex, and horizontal tokens in different layers are distinct.' Second review: 'COMPLETENESS IN THE ORDER pays count sufficiency'."),
("C27","The increment kernel is reflection-equivariant: K(rho s, rho t) = K(s,t).","inputs/author-CANDIDATE.md","Full ordinary proof","'It obeys K(rho s,rho t)=K(s,t), by swapping X,Y and preserving Z.'"),
("C28","The count difference changes by at most one, giving no crossing.","inputs/author-CANDIDATE.md","Full ordinary proof","'Also its count difference changes by at most one, since U,V are bits. Therefore no one-step transition from a>b ends at a<b, nor conversely.'"),
("C29","Reflected mass dominance is preserved by the paired-sum identity.","inputs/author-CANDIDATE.md","Full ordinary proof","Displayed identity: Delta(muK)(t) = sum_s mu(s)[K(s,t)-K(s,rho t)] = sum_{s above} Delta mu(s)[K(s,t)-K(s,rho t)] = sum_{s above} Delta mu(s)K(s,t) >= 0."),
("C30","The initial distribution satisfies reflected mass dominance.","inputs/author-CANDIDATE.md","Full ordinary proof","'The initial distribution satisfies this condition, so induction gives it at every prefix.'"),
("C31","The conditional payoff is g(a,b) = (2^-b - 2^-a)/2.","inputs/author-CANDIDATE.md","Full ordinary proof","'g(a,b) := E(U-V | a,b) = (1/2)(2^{-b}-2^{-a}).'"),
("C32","g is antisymmetric, zero on the diagonal and nonnegative above it.","inputs/author-CANDIDATE.md","Full ordinary proof","'The function g is antisymmetric, zero on the diagonal and nonnegative above it.'"),
("C33","At index v, E[U-V] is the difference of the two connection probabilities.","inputs/author-CANDIDATE.md","Full ordinary proof","'Taking k=v-1 proves the desired connection probability inequality for u<v.'"),
("C34","For v<u both probabilities are zero; for v=u they are 1 and 1/2; n=0 is vacuous.","inputs/author-CANDIDATE.md","Full ordinary proof","'If v<u, both probabilities are zero by monotonicity of indices. If v=u, the same-layer probability is one and the other is 1/2. ... n=0 has no endpoint pairs.'"),
("C35","General acyclic digraphs lack count sufficiency; a concrete obstruction exists.","inputs/shortest-proof-PROOF.md","A genuinely broader consequence","'A missing predecessor changes q^a into q^(number of reachable predecessors). ... take a later vertex whose only predecessor is x: a prefix reaching x0 but not y0 and one reaching y0 but not x0 have equal counts, yet different entry probabilities.'"),
("C36","Adding missing arcs to form a tournament changes the probabilities and no monotonicity of their difference is available.","inputs/second-review-REVIEW.md","Section 2","'Every DAG embeds in a tournament order, but adding missing arcs changes both connection probabilities and their difference has no available monotonicity.'"),
("C37","The column-homogeneous extension uses p(j), q(j), Z(j) and payoff g(j)(a,b).","inputs/shortest-proof-PROOF.md","A genuinely broader consequence","'The same proof works conditional on ANY fixed post set T, with independent horizontal probabilities p_j in [0,1] shared by every incoming arc i->j and both layers. Then Z_j=1_(j in T), q_j=1-p_j ... and g_j=(1-Z_j)(q_j^b-q_j^a).'"),
("C38","E7 is the p(j)=1/2 specialization of the column-homogeneous law.","inputs/shortest-proof-PROOF.md","A genuinely broader consequence","'The E7 endpoint is the p_j=1/2, independent fair-post specialization of this reviewer-authored extension.'"),
("C39","Reflection until meeting is an old technique (Aldous and Fill, Chapter 12, Section 12.1.8).","inputs/second-review-REVIEW.md","Section 1","'The reflection-until-meeting construction is an old technique.' The same paragraph cites 'Aldous-Fill Chapter12 section12.1.8'."),
("C40","Lean is 4.34.1 with mathlib revision d13f23b723b8a846827a245b89c10fc7d3f11612.","TASK.txt","CONTENT item 5","'Lean 4.34.1, mathlib d13f23b723b8a846827a245b89c10fc7d3f11612'. Also inputs/format-example.roff: 'Lean is 4.34.1 ... with mathlib revision d13f23b723b8a846827a245b89c10fc7d3f11612.'"),
("C41","The endpoint is theorem bunkbed_E7_transitive in namespace Bun.","inputs/lean/BunFinalEndpoint.lean","theorem bunkbed_E7_transitive","theorem bunkbed_E7_transitive (n : Nat) (u v : Fin n) : Fintype.card {ω : Out n // Reach n ω (u, false) (v, true)} ≤ Fintype.card {ω : Out n // Reach n ω (u, false) (v, false)} := by"),
("C42","card_token states Fintype.card (Token n) = n*n and card_out states Fintype.card (Out n) = 2^(n*n).","inputs/lean/BunFinalModel.lean","theorem card_token and theorem card_out","theorem card_token (n : Nat) : Fintype.card (Token n) = n * n := by; theorem card_out (n : Nat) : Fintype.card (Out n) = 2 ^ (n * n) := by"),
("C43","The axioms are exactly propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.","inputs/r23-audit-output.txt","#print axioms output","'Bun.bunkbed_E7_transitive' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. The same three appear for window_factor, card_pairLt, card_htoken, card_token, card_out, prob_layer_true_le_false, state_endpoint and stf_reach_endpoint; reach_of_lt uses [propext, Quot.sound]."),
("C44","33 modules were rebuilt from an empty build.","TASK.txt","CONTENT item 5","'that 33 modules were rebuilt from an empty build'."),
("C45","The Reach bridge is Bun.stf_reach_endpoint, with strong form Bun.stf_reach_strong.","inputs/lean/BunReachBridge.lean","theorem stf_reach_endpoint and theorem stf_reach_strong","stf_reach_endpoint: ((v : Nat) ∈ sval σ (stf n (u : Nat) (v : Nat) (wres n (v : Nat) ω))) ↔ Reach n ω (u, false) (v, σ). stf_reach_strong adds the guard (u : Nat) ≤ (i : Nat) ∧ (i : Nat) ≤ j."),
("C46","The state-level inequality is Bun.state_endpoint.","inputs/lean/BunDomFinal.lean","theorem state_endpoint","theorem state_endpoint : ∀ (n u j : Nat), u ≤ j → j < n → Fintype.card {w : Bun.Asg n j // j ∈ Bun.sval true (Bun.stf n u j w)} ≤ Fintype.card {w : Bun.Asg n j // j ∈ Bun.sval false (Bun.stf n u j w)} := by"),
("C47","The counting bridge is Bun.window_factor.","inputs/lean/BunFinalWindow.lean","theorem window_factor","Fintype.card {ω : Out n // P (wres n j ω)} = 2 ^ Fintype.card (outside n j) * Fintype.card {w : Asg n j // P w}."),
("C48","The prior-art search was bounded.","inputs/second-review-REVIEW.md","Section 4","'Bounded 2024-2026 later-literature search'; 'No full citation graph, all repositories, non-English literature or worldwide absence was established.'"),
("C49","The final journal version of Przybylowski's paper (DOI 10.1016/j.ejc.2025.104289) was not read.","TASK.txt","CONTENT item 6","'the final journal version of Przybylowski's paper (DOI 10.1016/j.ejc.2025.104289) was not read'. Author proposal: 'The ScienceDirect 403 is retained as a gap, with no retry.'"),
("C50","No acceptance, peer review, priority or worldwide novelty is claimed.","TASK.txt","INTEGRITY RULES and CONTENT","'Do not claim acceptance, peer review, priority or worldwide novelty.' The paper states the same in the abstract and Section 6."),
("C51","The draft was prepared with AI assistance; authorship is to be determined.","TASK.txt","INTEGRITY RULES","'Write the author line as: \"Draft prepared with AI assistance; authorship to be determined.\"'"),
("C52","Hollom reference details: Lawrence Hollom, The bunkbed conjecture is not robust to generalisation, arXiv:2406.01790 (2024), European Journal of Combinatorics 128 (2025) 104188.","inputs/literal382297.json; inputs/sources/bunkbed-journal.txt","source_name field; journal page header","literal382297.json source_name: 'Lawrence Hollom, \"The bunkbed conjecture is not robust to generalisation\", arXiv:2406.01790 (2024).' Journal header: 'L. Hollom European Journal of Combinatorics 128 (2025) 104188'."),
("C53","Przybylowski reference details: Tomasz Przybylowski, The acyclic directed bunkbed conjecture is false, arXiv:2506.22284v2 (11 November 2025).","inputs/sources/bunkbed-acyclic.txt","page header","'arXiv:2506.22284v2 [math.CO] 11 Nov 2025'; title 'The acyclic directed bunkbed conjecture is false'; author 'Tomasz Przybyłowski'."),
("C54","van Hintum-Lammers reference details: Peter van Hintum and Piet Lammers, The bunkbed conjecture on the complete graph, arXiv:1803.07647v4 (27 March 2021).","inputs/sources/bunkbed-complete-correct.txt","page header","'arXiv:1803.07647v4 [math.CO] 27 Mar 2021'; title 'The bunkbed conjecture on the complete graph'; authors Peter van Hintum and Piet Lammers."),
("C55","Aldous-Fill details: Chapter 12, Section 12.1.8.","inputs/second-review-REVIEW.md","Section 1","'Aldous-Fill Chapter12 section12.1.8'."),
]
out={"paper":"The bunkbed conjecture for transitive tournaments","mathdb":"382297","claims":[{"id":c[0],"claim":c[1],"source":c[2],"locator":c[3],"support":c[4]} for c in claims]}
open("qa/tmp/CLAIMS.json","w",encoding="utf-8").write(json.dumps(out,ensure_ascii=False,indent=2))
print("claims",len(claims))
